notes.title: Chefs from every far corner of the universe! We are here to deliver a fix for a bug preventing progression when serving orders in your restaurant.

items.text: Order Serving Rewards: Fixed a bug where serving an order occasionally caused an error that prevented players from receiving their rewards. The following will now update correctly upon serving:
Money and XP.
Gastropedia "Served" counts.
Achievement progress (including Serve 500 Customers and Serve All Recipes).
Optional Goal progress (e.g., Serve Common Dishes).

Additionally, we fixed an issue where a group of 2 or more customers would sometimes order an item when you only had one left in stock. Now, they will leave if you don't have enough servings to match the group size.

We’re excited to roll out a major post-launch update for Space Chef, packed with fixes, polish, and quality-of-life improvements based directly on your feedback. From the moment we launched, you’ve been helping us track bugs, suggest changes, and share both what you love and what could be better. This update is our way of saying thank you.
We’ve been overwhelmed (in the best way!) by the positivity in your reviews. It means the world to our small team to see thousands of players enjoying the game we’ve poured nearly seven years into.

A lot of you wrote a positive review hoping that we would fix some things in a future update, and that's what this update is all about. We've really tried to read and analyze all reviews, both positive and negative, all forum posts and all Discord threads.

notes.title: Can't wait to play? Then play right now!

items.text: The update is out as you read this. Just start Steam and let it update, and get cooking!
Check out the video covering the patch here!
[dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=imEGAZF3nBw"]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1272290/Space_Chef"]

notes.title: A quick summary of all the things we've updated

items.text: Quality of life updates and new features
Better progression clarity
Faster progression, less grind
Less frustration and spoilage
Things are now more durable
Things are now less expensive
Machines and restaurant mechanics are easier to understand
Major bug fixes
For the juicy details, keep reading!

notes.title: Quality of life updates and new features

items.text: There are some things that a lot of you were asking for, and we're incredibly happy to be able to offer these things:
You asked for it, and we hereby give you… a larger inventory! When you reach 2 stars, you unlock 30 inventory slots!
You can craft and cook items when away from home, as long as you have the materials.
You can remove items from the food menu with a simple click on the menu
Hovering over a crate now shows a preview of what's inside
The quest tracker now switches to the quest you just made progress on
Pin a recipe/blueprint and have it easily accessible on the left side
You can cancel restaurant orders
If your restaurant has more than 6 customers, you'll get more time per order
Yes, we were a little too confident in our own cleverness when doing the puzzles in the game. We’d hoped for a fun and mysterious sense of progression, but instead got a bit of a cryptic mess.

All upcoming blueprints to be unlocked while levelling up skills are now shown in the Gastropedia —o more surprises! It’s a lot easier to know what skills you need to progress, to get those Advanced Solar Panels or a Gas Gun.
Each NPC's current location can now be seen in the Gastropedia. No need to run around hunting and discovering empty locations.
We rewrote all 33 quest descriptions to make them clearer and added some hints to make it a lot easier to progress without spoiling too much
We added a total of 12 new radio messages that give hints about things like machetes, pickaxes, robot dogs, alien gas, quartz and last but not least: Marty's Top 5 Energizing Drinks.

This is a tricky one, as a lot of you enjoyed the slow and steady pace, but a lot of other players thought that the game progressed too slowly and were impatient to see what's next. Being able to reach the Outer Zone faster was a common request.
All skills and reputation now increase faster, meaning less grind to unlock new blueprints
Advanced Solar Panels, at Reputation 1.5 stars
Moltron Solar Panels, at Reputation 3 stars
Slow Cooker, at Cooking 4
Space Suit, at Exploration 5
For the complete picture, check the new Gastropedia view!
You now get bonus XP for longer distance orders on the Outer and Far Zone
Gas is now a lot faster to harvest, and you get more, especially Nitrogen
You can also get Fusion Batteries from Electric Junk, from broken Satellites
The Bontha now is easier to find, and gives you more Bontha Meat if you manage to hunt it
There were some things here and there that frustrated you. We hope that the fixes below will make it a less frustrating and a more pleasant experience.
Food takes a lot longer to spoil
All processed and cooked meals start spoiling in 24 hours, then go from the starting quality to completely spoiled in 48 hours
Note that the 48 hours is based on 5 star starting quality. For lower quality ingredients/meals, the spoil time is reduced proportionally. The time to start spoiling is always 24 hours.
Items in fridges lasts 4-5 times longer
Ship handling and space travel have been adjusted
Added a ship braking setting which lets you stop the ship from drifting so much
Improved UFO and Nebula Storm chaser rotation speed
Reduced asteroid collision damage a lot
Pirates attack less frequently
Disassembly drones spawn less frequently
Combat is smoother
Fixed an issue when spamming the attack button, which made you attack slower
Fixed another issue when you spammed attack, and turned the other way, the player would keep attacking in the wrong direction
The Polka Snake and other animals that hide should stay out for a little longer, most of the time
Remember, use RS or mouse to aim when you attack! ⚔️
Farming in the start is easier
You can no longer delete Plant Box (and also Fridge) by mistake until the blueprints are unlocked
General store now have a chance of selling Rushwood as well as the seeds
You can now get free soil in the park without a shovel
All craftable weapons now last longer
All machines last longer
Hull plating Level 2 lasts longer in the Toxic Cloud
Hull plating Level 3 doesn't take damage in the Toxic Cloud
Decorations are now cheaper
Adding floorplans is now a LOT cheaper
Lowered ship repair cost
Lowered booster refuel cost
Tweaked some ship accessories prices at the ship store
Towing and repairs of your spaceship when damaged in space is cheaper
Lowered intensity of cold effect on Crystalia
Underwater air time on Bluegoonia lasts slightly longer
Lowered sun damage
Lowered Gnibbits damage
The "Flip!" and "Ready!" when cooking is now better in sync with the perfect position

notes.title: Machines and restaurant mechanics are easier to understand

items.text: Added speech bubbles to Compost, Water Tank and other machines to explain how to use them
Added a message when you need to clean the restaurant table if it's preventing you from getting customers
Fixed a glitch where the chef could walk through some plants and also teleporting back when that happened
Caveron out of bounds issue and getting to the wrong floor when dying causing confusion
Fixed Snowbell quest where it needed 12 glass to complete
Fixed an issue where creating a lot of machines made time stop at home
Fixed an issue where the space ship sometimes suddenly drove towards the sun
Fixed "Food trends" disappearing after changing scene
Fixed various issues with picking up the drops after hunting larger animals
Loads of other minor bug fixes

notes.title: Stuck? Here's how to get unstuck!

items.text: There might still be some issues where you can get stuck, but you can use emergency respawn, now also on gamepads:
Keyboard: CTRL-SHIFT-K three times
For gamepads and Steam Deck (LT+RT+LB+RB and press B, three times)
We're really happy with this update, and we think it feels much more polished. We hope it makes your time in the Horseshoe Nebula smoother, cozier, and even more satisfying.

We worked with a porting house to create Space Chef’s console versions. This allowed us to bring the game to far more places than we’d otherwise have been able to, but it also introduces cost and complexity to updating those versions. This is one of those ‘reality of game development’ trade-offs. Unfortunately, it's currently extremely unlikely that we'll be able to bring this update to PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch. Rest assured we're trying our best to make it happen, and we'll update you if anything changes.

This update is the last planned major patch for Space Chef. That said: we’re not closing the doors for potential future updates and we will definitely be engaged in the community for as long as there are players. Here are some ways to engage with us developers and the community:
The Space Chef Discord is full of friendly chefs and explorers.

The Space Chef Wiki on Fandom is alive and growing and has a complete list of all the recipes, blueprints, characters, creatures and everything else in the game. Feel free to contribute with your own content and add tips on various pages to share with other players.
The Steam Discussion Forum has a lot of great posts with questions, tips and tricks
We will always be around to answer questions, or just talk about angry Gnibbits!

We're incredibly proud of what we’ve made, and so grateful to each of you who helped shape this game into what it is today. Thank you for playing, for backing, and for believing in our weird, ambitious idea about cooking in space. ❤️
– The Space Chef Team

topNew: There are some things that a lot of you were asking for, and we're incredibly happy to be able to offer these things:
You asked for it, and we hereby give you… a larger inventory! When you reach 2 stars, you unlock 30 inventory slots!
You can craft and cook items when away from home, as long as you have the materials.

items.text: Grab your ladles and tell your squad - Steam Next Fest is right around the corner, and the Space Chef Demo is crash-landing onto the front page like a flaming souffle on June 9!
This is the biggest chance yet to get new players hooked on cooking, looting, space-scootering, and (accidentally) setting the grill on fire. So do us a favor and spread the word like spilled gravy:
Tell your friends
Tell your coworkers
Tell that one cousin who only plays fishing simulators
Tell your cat (they won’t care, but still)
Every wishlist, every playthrough, every thumbs-up helps our spicy little indie game stand out in a galaxy full of bland gruel.

notes.title: Oops! I dropped it again - Death drop system

items.text: Lost all your ingredients cause you messed with the wrong Graffle? Again!? No more! Now when your health hits zero, you'll just take a quick nap. Don't snooze too long though... You've got three days to return and reclaim your precious ingredients and materials. Bags are clearly marked on your map, radar, and minimap, so losing track of them is practically impossible unless you're deliberately avoiding responsibility (like the old "Keep Inventory" toggle, may it rest in peas).

notes.title: Love hurts? Try this one romantic trick!

items.text: Struggling to impress your cosmic crush? Whip up the legendary Buzziecoa Love Pralines! But be warned, it's not as easy as it sounds. You’ll have to battle sea monsters for Jelly Drops, face stone golems for the juicy Pearfect, and brave Crystalia's blizzard for Crystal Fruit. If that sounds too intense, maybe just stick with Beefle Skewers...
The upside? Buzziecoa Love Pralines never spoil, unlike some relationships we know.
Each NPC has five increasingly rare favorite foods. Impress them all, choose your words wisely, and they'll say yes faster than you can say "Greasy Ratoid Plate with a side of Shimmer Dippers".

notes.title: May the force be with chew - Space gameplay revamp

items.text: Space just got spicy! We've revamped cosmic adventures so you’ll encounter more events and hazards in your path, making space travel feel alive and reactive. Brace yourself for asteroids, pirates, and nasty disassembly drones eager to "disassemble" your plans. Upgrade your defenses, your future self will thank you.

Your first scooter now also zooms faster and even has a built-in mini booster for speedy deliveries or quick escapes from pirates or your responsibilities. Plus, we added flashy "Whoosh Zoom Kablam" smoke effects to trick your brain into believing you’re flying even faster, science approved!
Oh, and when you take a "space-nap" (exploding in bits and pieces), your stuff conveniently floats for easy pick-up later. Unless pirates get it first!

notes.title: Order upgrades - Cooking without the cookbook!

items.text: Order tooltips are now clearer than broth on simmer, displaying required ingredients for each dish right where you need them. Forget fumbling between Rainbow Salads and Root Salads, unless fumbling is your secret sauce.

Is setting up your restaurant menus unclear? Restaurant open/close confusing? We know! That's why we've packed the game with helpful tutorials right from the start! But if you're the click-happy type that don't read anything (Hey, you're reading this, aren't you?), check the Gastropedia for everything you missed.

Plus, NPC radio hints now guide you toward vital materials like coal and ice. If you go full Beefle-slayer and defeat 30 of them in one morning, your spatula will snap like a dry twig. Look no further, a helpful tutorial will walk you through crafting a new one before it’s too late. Keep up the Beefle bashing!

Yes, you can milk certain animals - surprise to some, we're sure, as it wasn't very clear before! Our favorite nebula biologist, J'Sie Saster, broadcasts useful creature tips and milking etiquette (spoiler: some animals prefer their personal space).
You're able to track your culinary conquests in the gastropedia, and these nifty little stars will show you how hard you've been working to make a dish popular:
Bronze star - Your dish debut!
Silver star - Served 10 times, nice!
Golden star - Served 25 times, hot stuff!
Moltron star - Served 50 times, legendary chef territory!
Keep your menu fresh - repeat dishes bore customers. Variety is the spice of nebula life!
58 thrilling achievements await, from cooking 100 meals to conquering a Bontha with nothing but a spatula. Talk about flipping awesome!

Your storage boxes got an upgrade - sturdy, spacious, and customizable with fun colors. Sizes range from the cozy small (6 slots) to the roomy medium (12 slots), and the massive large box (18 slots). Storage has never looked so good.
Sick of trekking to Hiro in Glimmerrock just to switch ships? So were we. Introducing the Ship Switcher! Now switch between all your ships comfortably from home.

releases.displayName: Chef Update: Cooking up a Love Story

notes.title: Space is often a lonely voyage, where a sole space chef can find themselves longing for an interplanetary partner.

items.text: This Valentine's Day we’re looking at romance in Space Chef and how you can make the void of space a lot more romantic.
If this all looks a little familiar to our last announcement, then read to the end for some exclusive tips on how to romance the scrappy, Zoe!
There are over 30 NPCs that are now complete, boasting around 30,000 words of dialogue and a whole bunch of interesting sounds and emotions to go with their colorful personalities.

Each NPC has a distinct personality and storyline, with five of them being romanceable. The romance system has been expanded to include a unique progression path for each character - woo your favorites by gifting them their unique loved dishes.
Besides romance, each character has their own interests and plots and quests which also is a great way to get to know them better.
The romance system now comes with a heart-based visual indicator in the Gastropedia, making it easier than ever to track your progress with each character. Here’s how it works:
Transparent Heart - You haven’t given this NPC their unique gift yet. Time to find out what they like!
Normal Heart - You’ve given the NPC one unique gift, and they’re starting to warm up to you. This means that there are new dialog options available.
Big Heart - You’re one step closer to becoming partners - keep those gifts coming!
Pounding Hearts - You're now partners!
When new dialog options are enabled, you need to choose your words wisely to advance your relationship. However, most of the time, you can always try again another day.
A friendly warning though…
Some choices you make might make the NPC and romance opportunity disappear for good, so be careful with your action...
Want to romance multiple persons?
Go ahead, we're not judging, but there might be someone watching with their big ears. We're not saying any names here…
The scrap mechanic, Zoe is fond of a sweat treat! Don't let her hard-look exterior fool you, Zoe is as sweet as they come, with dreams and ambitions that would lead her beyond Rusty Town.
One of her five favorite foods is something you bake, and it's orange with green dots. Can you figure out what it is?

releases.displayName: Chef Update: It's Looking Sunny Side Up!

items.text: We’re back with a fresh batch of updates, improvements, and sneak peeks to share with you. Your feedback and support have been fantastic and are helping shape the final version of Space Chef.

We’re thrilled to announce that Space Chef has officially entered a proper Alpha stage, meaning that all main features and content are complete. There are still a lot of bugs to squash, and even more polish to be made.
We're also doing tweaks to the UI and feedback, to increase the satisfaction when you've worked like crazy to get a unique and mythical recipe to another happy customer.
The delicious Shimmerspores on Caveron can only be harvested by walking nearby and triggering an explosion. But watch out, the Splittler isn't too happy to see you in the caves!

Right now we’re focusing on making the first 30 minutes of the game as exciting and engaging as possible, and giving a taste of the rest of the game. We want every player to experience an adventure packed with exploration, cooking, and a few surprises along the way.

We’ve been paying close attention to feedback on our death and inventory mechanics. Many of you suggested adding a "Keep Inventory" setting, which we added, but we're still discussing it - should it be left in the game, or should we replace it with a "drop stuff where you die, so you can go back and pick it up" feature?
We want a perfect balance of challenge and fun and make it feel rewarding for risk-takers without making it too easy for the faint of heart. Balance, balance, balance…

Another feature we recently added is the "I'm about to die" UI effect that covers the edges of the screen. A similar effect is shown when you're about to freeze to death or get cooked by the Cyclonian heat. And don't forget about dying of lack of oxygen or getting poisoned. There are so many ways to die, and we can't wait to see you try them all out!
Notice the red outlines of the screen? You will if you keep fighting wildlife with that Dull Knife!

One of our goals is making sure Space Chef looks great no matter where you’re playing - from a small Steam Deck screen to the widest of ultrawide monitors. We’ve refined our UI to make everything look crisp and fitting seamlessly across different resolutions.
See more on the sides on a wider screen, as we're supporting up to 21:9 monitors. Even wider monitors work of course, but will have black bars on the sides, to avoid spoiling too much...

notes.title: New delivery UI and special orders

items.text: To make it more worthwhile to discover and deliver new dishes, and always keeping your menu fresh, we're currently working on a new system that keeps track of what you serve.

This has the effect that if you just keep serving those Beefle Skewers, after a while, you will get less and less reputation for each order, until your customer won't order anything from you. Guess what, it's time to refresh your menu!

To visualize this and to make it clear when you're doing something great, we've added this new bouncy delivery report that shows the quality and the popularity of what you just served, among other things.
We're also planning on adding stats to Gastropedia, so you can easily keep track of what's hot and what's not and what you've been delivering so far.
Work in progress of the new food delivery stats

Another thing to keep things fresh, is that we’re working on adding a variety of Special Orders that come with special bonuses. Think rush orders, pirate encounters, VIP orders and even long-distance challenges.
Every now and then, an order comes to keep you on your toes, with opportunities to build even more reputation and meet new customers across the void of space.

A little tease for the explorers among you! Some planets have mysterious ruins that you may have come across. At first glance, they’re inactive, but apparently, there is some way to activate them… What could be lurking there? Delicious ancient food? Ancient spoiled food? Whatever it is, it's ancient, and you'll have to play to find out!
If only you could hear the mysterious sound they make, I guess you'll have to come visit the Hum Dum Ruins.

We want Space Chef to reach as many players as possible by localizing the game in various languages. We've been hard at work putting each and every word and dialog in a giant database, and it currently has nearly 50,000 words!
We're still working out which languages the game will be available in, but we'll update you more on that later.
Sound design and dynamic music
Sound really makes you feel immersed in a world, and you can hear everything between a Gnibbit's yawn to a Graffles honk, or even the satisfying "plop" of UI icons popping up.
Our excellent sound designer Hugo, and our brilliant composer Paul have been working together to make Space Chef sound really good.
Nothing beats the sound of sizzling Ratoids on the grill

Did you notice that the music in your home is subtly different between day and night? And as you get further into space, the music changes as well. And we've recently added a special soundtrack when your restaurant is open.
Every detail matters in making Space Chef feel alive!

If you're one of the players who love unlocking achievements and finding everything there is to find in a game, we've got good news for you. We have hidden mysterious recipes and secret weapons, and we will also be adding lots of achievements later.
All this for you completionists who want to go all out and complete everything Space Chef has to offer.
So many empty slots. Wait, what, 144 recipes? I gotta cook 'em all!

releases.displayName: Today’s Forecast sees Brutal Sandstorms, Toxic Gas Clouds, and a Juicy Update!

items.text: You better grab your aprons, equip your homemade gas guns, and start working up an appetite, because it’s time for another update!

In this update, we’ll be revisiting the barren deserts of Cyclonia, talking about the weather (everyone’s favorite topic), and introducing a few new mechanics that we’re sure will make your transition to an interstellar lifestyle even smoother.
Over the summer, we’ve been cooking up a storm (Quite literally. We don't recommend bringing an umbrella). Here’s the cosmic scoop on what we’ve achieved in the past two months.

notes.title: Of Maps, Monsters, and Meteor Craters

items.text: Cyclonia has gone through a lot of changes and innovations since our original Kickstarter demo, which we’re very excited to share with you!
The full planet map has now been implemented, but will be shrouded in a fog of war. Or should we say a fog of please-explore? (Nailed it).

Every step you take, every move you make…will be tracked by unknown cosmic forces and result in a Location Discovered pop-up. Every time you find a new location, you’ll earn precious XP! That XP will automatically be sprinkled onto your Exploration skill, so you’ll be a well-seasoned space-traveler in no time.
But all of this exploration would be nothing without strange and horrifying alien creatures to meet with (and possibly make meat out of)!

From sentient cacti to two-headed snakes, Cyclonia is now rich with life. All of the local wildlife has now been added to the planet, so you’ll never be short of creatures to study, hunt, and run away from.

Each creature has its own unique behaviors, with some being nocturnal and some being diurnal. That’s a very fancy way of saying that some come out at night and others come out during the day. Don’t even ask us what crepuscular means.
We’ve also added a feature where special and legendary creatures will only spawn once you’ve reached a certain level, so you’ll have to up your game if you want to take down big game.

Alongside the biodiversity, we wanted to really spice up the terrain on Cyclonia, so we’ve dotted meteor craters, hot springs, natural bridges, and spaceship wrecks to give you that added sense of life-endangerment.

It’ll also allow you to climb to higher parts of the map, where you’ll find the Hornagle and their notoriously delicious eggs. We’ve heard they make an omelet worth dying for (which we’re sure will make for a comforting final thought when the Hornagle mother is eviscerating you).

notes.title: From Gas Planets to Windy Planets, a History of Far Out Flatulence

items.text: Remember when we made that joke earlier about “literally” cooking up a storm?
It’s finally time for the punchline!

From calm skies to raging sandstorms, we’ve introduced a weather system to Cyclonia. After all, everyone knows that the real key to developing a chef’s delicate palette is to constantly have a mouth full of sand. Certain areas of the map will also feature strong winds, which will challenge your navigational skills (and leave you wondering what kind of diet the locals have adopted to produce such an…explosive breeze).
You might think that rigid and dogmatic Health & Safety laws wouldn’t apply in the vast expanse of space.
And you’d be wrong!

Introducing our new elemental warning system. These handy symbols are designed to let you know key things about your current environment, such as when you’re overheating or when you’ve found yourself in a space station that has no oxygen. In retrospect, we realize that last one might be somewhat redundant, since by the time you’ve seen the no oxygen warning you’d already have, you know, suffocated…

Whenever the player enters an area with elemental hazards, the warning symbol will start to fill up. If you leave it for too long, it will begin flashing in a way that’s totally not stressful or anxiety inducing. Once the symbol is full, the player will start losing health and stamina. The only way to combat this is to either leave the area, which will result in the symbol slowly disappearing, or through the medium of…
Fashion!
Who needs to worry about subzero temperatures when you’ve got a nice coat?

Over time, you’ll be able to unlock elemental wearables, such as the Explorer’s Hat that will shield you from the blazing Cyclonian heat. This won’t remove the danger entirely, but will help you to withstand these elemental hazards for longer. If your budget doesn’t extend to the season’s latest trends, there will also be perishable items you can use to help with your weather woes. For example, eating Frostberries will cool you down (and have the added bonus of giving you perpetual brain freeze so you’ll have no energy left to think about how overheated you are).

If you’re fashion-less and Frostberry-less, however, there’s no need to panic. You’ll still be able to use food items to restore any health that you’ve lost as a result of elemental hazards. That being said, the last thing you want to do is end up munching all of the ingredients you risked your life to harvest!
We’ve made a few tweaks to the various spaceships you can find (for a small fee) throughout the universe, so they all handle slightly differently.
But what about the space-faring public?

You’ll now encounter civilian ships as you navigate through the vacuum of space. Just in case the ship design and engine exhaust doesn’t immediately give it away, you’ll be able to tell which direction they’re going in based on the trails behind them, so you can easily move out of their way (or stalk them, we won’t judge).

If you happen to get in their way, there’s a chance they will honk at you, and they may even make a witty comment as they drive by. If you crash into them, they will certainly have something to say about it, so all the more incentive to collide with your neighbors and see what hilarious commentary they will make as they are engulfed in the fiery wreckage of their beloved spaceship.
Also, as you become more famous, the chances increase that people will actually say something really nice to you.

notes.title: Don’t Just Pass Gas, Harvest It!

items.text: When you’re not busy crashing into the locals of Rusty Town, you’ll probably want to harvest the vast array of delights that space has to offer.
That’s why we’ve added some handy tools, so you can extend mankind’s desire to aggressively sap vital and limited resources into the final frontier!

The drill has been updated, so you can harvest precious rocks and minerals from a total of nine different asteroid types with ease, if you got the right drill that is. We’ve also added the gas skimmer, which will sap various types of gas straight from the atmosphere and into your inventory. It’s a tool that is sure to come in handy, whether you’re traveling through a gas cloud or simply dealing with the fallout of a bean binge.
But why should you want to be all gassed up?

Because gas is a very valuable resource! For example, carbon dioxide will add the fizz to your soft drinks, while propane can be used to fuel your grill. Or guns, but we don't recommend that. Unless you're a very violent person.

notes.title: Please Don’t Bite the Hand that Feeds

items.text: Are you one of those people who could spend hours feeding the ducks at their local park?
Then we’ve got just the mechanic for you!
Except the park is a dangerous otherworldly planet, the food requires hours of strenuous labor to harvest, and the ducks are colossal extraterrestrial creatures with teeth the size of your head.
So why should you be risking your life to give these alien beasts a snack?

While they’re distracted, you’ll be able to harvest valuable ingredients from them, such as the turthats shown on the back of the Turtosaurus (shown above) or the deliciously vague substance known only as “cream.”

notes.title: Warp-Speed Deliveries: Unlock the Power of The Ring Gates

items.text: When you’ve just received an order from the Inner Zone but you’re all the way out in the Far Zone, how are you ever going to make the delivery in 8 minutes or less?
With the help of portals, of course!
These portals will start off disabled, but will be activated as part of a key NPC quest. Once you’ve discovered all 4 portals, you’ll be able to navigate across the galaxy with ease!
To encourage players to serve a wide variety of delicacies, rather than just the same recipes over and over, we’ve added a special order mechanic!
These special orders will be unlocked once you reach a certain level, so you won’t be challenged too early on in your culinary journey. But what makes these orders so special?

The tricky thing is that the special order is always something that you don't have on your menu, you’ll get an extra whole 5 minutes of time, which should allow you to hunt down the new ingredients, cook up the new recipe, and deliver to the hungry customer. Sounds easy right? If you rise to the challenge, you’ll receive twice the reputation and double the amount of money as you would get from a normal order. That’s double the reward, double the fun, and double the increase in blood pressure!

notes.title: Keep Your Tongue on the Trends

items.text: You know what’s so hot right now?
No, no you don’t. But you will, with the help of your handy radio!

Once you get past a certain level, you’ll also unlock tips for all the trendiest treats. Every week, you’ll be informed by a random NPC via radio about that week’s trending food item. Much like Special Orders, if you accept and fulfill orders for that week’s trending recipe, you’ll receive double reputation and double the money. Now you’ll be able to carry on the grand corporate tradition of exploiting customers’ fear-of-missing-out in exchange for cold, hard cash.
We hope you’ve enjoyed this latest update, but there’s still plenty more to come.

Stay tuned on your space radio for our next transmission. In the meantime, we’d like to once again thank all of our backers for their ongoing support and we hope you’ll forgive us for making so many fart-based jokes in this update. We promise we’ll hold them in next time!
Want to keep up-to-date on the latest cosmic cuisine? 🍲

releases.displayName: New NPCs, Explorable Areas, and Recipes Await in Our Latest Update

notes.title: From new NPCs to spooky abandoned restaurants, we’ve got a big ol’ serving of new updates that we can’t wait for you to see! There’s a lot more behind-the-scenes that we weren’t able to include in this update, but we’ve selected the tastiest morsels for you to sink your teeth into.

items.text: Grab your knives and sporks, take a seat, and let’s tuck in!
With all of those asteroids to dodge and treacherous gas clouds to avoid, space feels like a dangerous and hostile place. So we thought, how can we make it seem a bit friendlier?
By adding space pirates, of course!
After all, what could warm you up better in the cold and unforgiving vacuum of space than a jolly old firefight with a group of hungry space pirates?

You’ll now meet bands of space pirates roaming around the cosmic sea in search of defenseless ships to plunder, so make sure you’ve got a few weapon attachments (or a knack for quick piloting and sharp turns!)

We’ve also added other NPCs out in space that are significantly less likely to steal your booty. At the moment, we can’t seem to stop them from flying into the sun and turning themselves into crispy metal bacon, but we’re hard at work putting in waypoints to protect all future space NPCs in our care.

notes.title: RIP Stands For Restaurants in Pieces

items.text: As you’re exploring the galaxy, you may stumble across some abandoned restaurants that shared the same mysterious fate as the one belonging to your grandma. What happened to them? Where are their owners? And, most importantly, what’s in it for you?

You’ll find all sorts of tasty treats inside these culinary crypts, including new recipes, new blueprints for items, inspiration for your home decor, and perhaps even some clues as to who might be behind these nefarious disappearances.

Alongside abandoned restaurants, we’ve also added a sunken spaceship on the planet Bluegoonia that might hide a deep sea-cret. Just remember to take your diving suit with you if you want to take a look at it, or you might end up sleeping with the mutant space fishes!
Our planet Cyclonia was looking a little tired, so we’ve given it a makeover!

Cyclonia is now made up of various different biomes, including vast deserts and barren rock terrain. When you make your first visit, your spaceship will land in Area 1 marked on the map below. But how do you make it to the other areas?

We’ll keep that a secret for now, but you’ll need to unlock new tools to reach them. We promise we’ll make it worth your while, as different areas will have new ingredients and creatures. Expanding your map means expanding your recipe book (or possibly dying in a brand new and exciting way!)
Don’t worry, we aren’t about to start our own charity!

We just wanted to treat our NPCs right and give them a comfortable place to lay down their heads at night after a long day of work. Can you guess which of our NPCs lives in this home with the luxurious Bontha-skin rug?

When you’re not out on the hunt for fresh new flavors, you’ll get to visit the homes of all of your favorite NPCs, with one exception: Officer Hoffman. After all, the best (and only) cop in the galaxy never has time to sleep! So we’ve begun building this cozy police station, where you can find him hard at work night and day.

Some of our public spaces didn’t feel quite as lively as we would have liked, so we’ve added a way for these scenes to become populated with NPCs over time. Now, when you want to take a peaceful stroll in the park, you won’t have a moment alone with your thoughts. How relaxing.

As you can see in the GIF below, we’ve added various tracks that our NPCs will follow and waypoints where they’ll perform certain actions, with each scene having a limit on how many NPCs can enter and exit at any given time. We’re fairly confident none of them will achieve sentience and realize their lives are being dictated by an inscrutable dev deity. Maybe don’t look them in the eyes when they walk past you though, just to be safe.

While you should always aim to provide service with a smile, sometimes even the greatest chef can feel worn down, hungry, or overcome with murderous rage. That’s why we’ve added new player animations to make movement look more natural and to make facial expressions more diverse!
Your chef will now look sad and tired when they’re feeling exhausted and may even let out a few yawns if they feel like you’re not paying enough attention.

notes.title: Putting the Model in Model Citizen

items.text: We’re getting all of our NPCs catwalk ready with stylish new outfits and character models to fit their size, shape, and personality. We’ve also adapted the way our basic character model works so various body parts can be scaled to fit different body types, such as children like Jenny, or longer pieces of clothing, such as Gloria’s dress.

We’ve updated our Gastropedia to make it look more authentic while still making it easy to use. Each of the tabs will lead to a different section, such as Creatures or Recipes, so you can keep track of everything you’ve discovered on your space adventure!
If you’re thinking there are a lot of food stains on those pages, you probably don’t want to see the state of our bookcases…

notes.title: Meat’s Back on the Menu, Boys!

items.text: In our last update, we introduced the planets of Crystalia and Bluegoonia. With new planets comes new creatures and with new creatures comes new… gastronomic opportunities. We’ll let you fill in the blanks on that one.

We’re employing fresh young talent to help us with development. In fact, our latest creature was designed by the daughter of lead developer Niclas. We want to get our kids all fired up about game design from a young age. Plus think of all the time and money we’ll save!
